text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday called for joint action to dismantle terrorism, asserting that there can be no justification for the scourge or double standards in tackling it, in a pointed message delivered in the presence of Pakistan’s deputy prime minister and defence minister Ishaq Dar at the 25th meeting of SCO council of heads of government at Dushanbe in Tajikistan .
“Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” Singh said in a thinly veiled swipe at Pakistan .
Also read: Ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively 'dismantled': Rajnath Singh at SCO meet
Terrorism, Singh said, poses a grave threat to peace and development, and its entire ecosystem must be collectively dismantled. India and Pakistan joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation as members in June 2017.
In his address, he stressed that connectivity must be based on “consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity” of all countries, arguing that “projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable.”
The comments are significant because New Delhi has long opposed the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) , a flagship project under China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), as a key section of the corridor passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). In the past, India has expressed concern at China and Pakistan using CPEC to alter the status quo in the region, and said the connectivity project passes through Indian territory that is under “forcible occupation” by Pakistan.
Also read: Future military power will depend on decision-making speed, not platform numbers: Rajnath Singh
“Connectivity is crucial for our shared prosperity. India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. Initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets,” he said.
Singh also highlighted the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region.
Economic engagement must be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all member states, he said. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States.”

Singh said the SCO must build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. There is a need to strengthen supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development, he said.
The meeting reviewed progress in multilateral economic and trade cooperation among SCO Member States and discussed measures to further strengthen cooperation in areas such as transport, finance, digital economy and social development, the defence ministry said in a statement.
Rahul Singh is Defence Editor at Hindustan Times and has covered military affairs and national security for nearly 25 years. Apart from extensive and deep reporting on the Indian military, including several newsbreaks that have set the national news agenda over the years, Rahul has reported from conflict zones including Jammu & Kashmir, India’s North-east and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Rahul has co-authored the bestselling 'India's Most Fearless' series of books on recent Indian military operations. Widely read and translated into multiple languages, the books place an emphasis on firsthand accounts of daring missions across the three services. His work has been adapted into web series and films including the National Award-winning Amaran. Rahul comes from an Army background and attended schools across the country before completing his education from Panjab University, Chandigarh.
